text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has decided to involve all domestic banks in disbursing agricultural credit by providing them a substantial return of 16 percent per annum.
- Citibank will provide 4.5 billion rupees three-year working capital to Kot Addu Power Company Ltd, now owned by British-based National Power.
- Pakistan and Germany have started talks to resolve important bilateral tax issues.
- Pakistan has invited expressions of interest for the privatisation of Pak Arab Fertilisers Ltd.
- Two Pakistan Air Force employees were convicted of smuggling contraband by a court martial on Thursday.
- Foreign ministry officials of Pakistan and India have made initial contacts and are laying the groundwork for the scheduled secretary-level talks to be held in New Delhi next month.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The State Bank has denied any move to enhance the mark-up rate on agricultural production loans.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has directed the Health Ministry to cancel the licences of all local and multi-national pharmaceutical companies which have provided 25 to 30 sub-standard and spurious samples during the past four years.
FINANCIAL POST
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said the government would change the destiny of the nation within its mandated period.
THE NEWS
- The government has established a special committee to review all the power sector contracts signed with independent power producers (IPPs).
- The Foreign Office denied that Pakistan had made any contact with Israel on the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty.
- The Election Commission is examining the British system of proxy voting to extend voting rights to overseas Pakistanis.
THE MUSLIM
- The opposition Pakistan People's Party has filed two references against the Minister for Social Welfare and Population Planning on charges of corruption.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
